title: Pneumonia, lung abscess, empyema and respiratory arrest in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the main lung condition (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Dysphagia and acute choking episode.

Vitals: BP 135/82, HR 78, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever or chills.
Respiratory: Positive for choking episode; negative for shortness of breath.
Gastrointestinal: Positive for dysphagia.
Neurological: Negative for weakness or confusion.

HPI: Patient is a 78-year-old male who presented to the emergency department after an episode of choking on a piece of meat. He reported a brief period of respiratory arrest which was managed by first responders. He was transported to the hospital for observation and evaluation of his swallowing function.

Hospital Course: The patient was admitted for observation. During his stay, he experienced a brief respiratory arrest while attempting to consume liquids. The medical team intervened immediately to clear the airway. Bag-mask breathing was initiated and successfully restored oxygenation. He made a full recovery from this event. No further complications occurred. He was cleared for a modified diet.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Choking episode
2. Dysphagia

Discharge Medications:
- Atrovent inhaler as needed
- Multivitamin daily

Follow-up: Speech therapy appointment scheduled for 05/20/2026.

Electronically signed,
R. Mensah, MD
05/15/2026
refs: ICD-10-CM Tabular: J15-J18, J69, J85-J86, R09

distractors.why: Respiratory failure is not documented; the arrest is.
